title: APSQ: Additive Partial Sum Quantization with Algorithm-Hardware Co-Design
problem: Input/weight stationary DNN accelerators suffer from excessive memory bandwidth and power consumption due to high-precision partial sum (PSUM) storage and retrieval, accounting for ~69% of power in typical dataflows.
motivation: PSUM quantization has been overlooked in prior compression strategies despite dominating memory and power costs in specialized DNN accelerators.
method: APSQ integrates PSUM accumulation into the quantization framework, compressing partial sums to INT8 through grouping and reconfigurable hardware support. The method performs nearly lossless compression on BERT, Segformer, and EfficientViT models by seamlessly combining PSUM quantization with algorithm-level optimizations.
key_novelty: First systematic approach to PSUM quantization as a primary compression target alongside weight/activation quantization in DNN accelerators.
contributions: APSQ algorithm compressing partial sums to INT8 with near-lossless accuracy on NLP and CV tasks
Reconfigurable architecture supporting PSUM grouping and quantization
28-87% energy reduction demonstrated across BERT, Segformer, EfficientViT, and LLaMA2-7B
limitations: Evaluation limited to relatively small models (BERT, EfficientViT) and single LLM variant (LLaMA2-7B); scalability to larger foundation models not fully explored.
primary_theme: Partial sum quantization for dataflow accelerators
